sights.w: Punggol's only mosque (2015, capacity 4,000), designed by Formwerkz Architects as an 'open mosque': a porous, naturally ventilated village cluster of prayer hall, school and offices around landscaped courts — widely published as a model of contemporary Singapore mosque architecture.
sights.k: Visitors welcome outside prayer times; dress modestly

sights.address: Punggol Promenade, between Punggol Point and Tebing Lane, Punggol, Singapore
sights.w: The waterfront park connector along Punggol's northern shore: the 2.4-km Nature Walk with fishing platforms and shelters on the Johor Strait, and the 1.2-km Riverside Walk with lookouts over Serangoon Reservoir ending at the Tebing Lane food cluster — linking Punggol Point Park to Punggol East. Wheelchair-friendly, best at sunset.
sights.k: Free; walk or cycle Punggol Point → Riverside Walk → dinner at Tebing Lane

sights.address: Punggol Coast, Punggol Way, Singapore (beside Punggol Coast MRT)
sights.w: Singapore's first 'enterprise district' (~50 ha, phase 1 opened from Q3 2024), marketed as Singapore's "Silicon Valley" and built around the Singapore Institute of Technology's new Punggol campus (classes from Sept 2024); the BCA Green Mark Platinum campus runs on 20,000+ sensors and smart lamp-posts. Campus Heart houses the SIT Visitor Gallery.
sights.k: SIT Visitor Gallery; pair with Punggol Coast Hawker Centre

sights.address: Old Punggol Road, Punggol Waterway Park (Heritage Zone), Punggol, Singapore
sights.w: A 1.5-km stretch of the original Punggol Road pedestrianised as a heritage trail in tribute to Punggol's past as a Teochew and Catholic kampong district of farms and fishing villages; reached via the Kelong Bridge, which recalls those fishing villages. A quiet walk through the before-the-new-town Punggol.
sights.k: Free; enter from the Kelong Bridge in Punggol Waterway Park

sights.address: Punggol Point Park, end of Punggol Point Road, Punggol, Singapore
sights.w: A long-standing, iconic jetty at Punggol Point — the coast of kelongs such as the 1969 Sea Palace kelong restaurant-cum-nightclub on stilts that made Punggol Point a seafood-and-leisure destination; NHB names Punggol Jetty among Punggol's heritage landmarks. Views to Pulau Ubin and the Johor Strait.
sights.k: Free; sunset; combine with Punggol Point Park

sights.w: HDB's new-generation neighbourhood centre on the Punggol Waterway (opened 2018–19), designed by Serie Architects with Multiply Architects as a stepped garden of terraces cascading to the water, with a rooftop community garden and polyclinic — published internationally by Dezeen and designboom. Houses Lao Jiang Superior Soup and Rise & Grind.
sights.k: Free; climb the terraces to the rooftop garden for waterway views
